dedupe_keys.name: traffic sample with zipf distributed mice and elephant flows

description: Hernández, José Alberto and colleagues document this resource in the B5G-OPEN community. The deposit is titled as a Zipf-distributed mice-and-elephant traffic sample, but its full description identifies code for theoretical Count-Min Sketch dimensioning examples. Its associated study provides rules for 100 and 400 Gb/s monitoring and evaluates P4 packet-optical-node implementations. Coverage is telemetry processing in metro networks. The sample-generation/example-code role is preserved; no independently observed carrier traffic dataset is inferred from the title. The code and physical testbed may have different execution requirements. Zenodo provides the deposited collection and native file inventory with open access; its stated licence is cc-by-4.0. File descriptors were inspected; the contents were not downloaded or executed. A limitation is that the native metadata do not establish all implementation settings, uncertainty bounds or independent reproducibility. Only descriptive metadata were inspected. Related records and companion papers retain their source-defined roles; they do not imply independent measurements. The examples support dimensioning the telemetry sketch used to monitor high-rate packet networks.
